quality_assessment: Good comprehensive coverage with clear examples, but contains several factual errors about file type definitions that could mislead users

issues.description: Documentation incorrectly lists *.pyw as part of Python type
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove *.pyw from the Python type description at line 38

issues.description: CSS type description is misleading - doesn't clarify that *.scss is shared with sass type
issues.current_content: **Note:** There is a separate `sass` type that includes *.sass and *.scss files.
issues.should_be: **Note:** Both the `css` and `sass` types include *.scss files. The `css` type includes *.css and *.scss, while the `sass` type includes *.sass and *.scss. When searching with -t css or -t sass, *.scss files will be included in both cases.
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify at line 300 that *.scss files are included in both css and sass types to avoid confusion

issues.description: PHP type definition is incomplete - missing *.php7, *.php8, and *.pht extensions
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 293 to include all PHP extensions supported by ripgrep

issues.description: Missing explanation of when glob patterns take precedence over types
issues.fix_suggestion: The section 'Type Filtering Precedence' (line 407) mentions this but could be clearer. Consider adding an explicit callout that glob patterns always override type selections.

issues.description: Type alias explanation could be clearer about how aliases work
issues.current_content: To see which types have aliases, check the output of `--type-list`. Types with aliases appear as `alias, fullname:` in the list.
issues.should_be: To see which types have aliases, check the output of `--type-list`. Types with aliases appear on the same line separated by commas (e.g., 'markdown, md:' or 'py, python:'), with all names referring to the same glob patterns.
issues.fix_suggestion: Provide a concrete example of what alias output looks like in --type-list at line 155
